title: वर्णधर्मानुशीलनम् [Caste practice]
nepali: ब्राह्मणाद्याश्चत्वारो वर्णाः सन्ति । वर्णव्यवस्थाया वर्णनं वेदस्मृतिपुराणादिषु ग्रन्थेषु सर्वत्र  विहितमुपलभ्यते । गृहस्थाश्रमवर्तीनां वर्णानां मध्ये ब्राह्मणानां साङ्गस्य वेदस्याध्यापनाध्ययने तथा यजनयाजने, दानप्रतिग्रहौ चेत्येतानि षट् कर्माणि शास्त्रेषु निरूपितानि सन्ति । तासु कर्मसु याजनाध्यापनप्रतिग्रहादीनि त्रीणि कर्माणि ब्राह्मणानां जीवनार्थानि मन्यन्ते । एवं वेदाध्ययनयजनदानादीनि त्रीणि कर्माणि ब्राह्मणानामिव क्षत्रियाणामपि कर्तव्यत्वेन निर्दिष्टानि सन्ति । अध्यापनयाजनप्रतिग्रहाख्यानि त्रीणि कर्माणि क्षत्रियाणां कृते निषिद्धानि मन्यन्ते । क्षत्रियाणां वृ¤यर्थं धर्मार्थञ्च प्रधानं कर्म प्रजापालनमेव निर्दिष्टमस्ति । एवं वैश्यस्य यागाध्ययनदानानि कुसीदकृषिवाणिज्यपशुपालनानि च कर्माणि वृ¤यर्थानि मन्यन्ते । शूद्रस्य तु धर्मार्थं वृ¤यर्थञ्च प्रधानं कर्म द्विजातीनां परिचर्यैव धर्मशास्त्रकारैर्मन्यते । अनेन प्रकारेण शास्त्रोक्तकर्मणा जीवितुमशक्नुवन्नापादि धर्मशास्त्रे आपद्धर्मस्य व्यवस्था विहिता वर्तते । तत्र चापदि ब्राह्मणः क्षत्रियकर्मणा, क्षत्रियो वैश्यकर्मणा तथा वैश्योऽपि शूद्रकर्मणा व्यवहर्तुं शक्नोति । एवं शुद्रोऽपि द्विजातीनां सेवया जीवितुमशक्नुवन्नापदि विविधशिल्पकर्मभिर्जीवेदिति व्यवस्था विहिता  वर्तते । वर्णेषु च जातिव्यवस्था प्रदर्शिता वर्तते । तत्र वर्णेषु जातानां द्वादशानां पुत्राणां मध्ये शास्त्रोक्तविवाहविधिमनुसृत्य विवाहितसवर्णकन्यायां जात एक एवौरसः पुत्रः सवर्णः सजातीयश्च मन्यते । वर्णानामनुलोमविवाहेषु क्रमिकरूपेण मूर्धावसिक्त–अम्बष्ठ–निषाद–माहिष्य–उग्र–करणाख्याः षडनुलोमजाः पुत्रा जायन्ते । धर्मशास्त्रे प्रतिलोमविवाहस्य विधिर्नास्ति । तथापि प्रतिलोमजाः सूत–वैदेहक–चण्डाल–मागध–क्षत्राऽयोगवाख्याः षट् पुत्रा तत्रापि भवन्ति । संकीर्णजातीनां परस्परकन्यासु जाताःपुक्कस–कुक्कुटक–क्षेत्ता–श्वपाक–वेण–सैरिन्ध्र–मैत्रेयक–मार्गव–चर्र्मकार–अन्ध्र–मेद–सोपाक–अन्त्यवसायी–पाण्डुसोपाक–आहिण्डिकादयो विविधाः पुत्रा भवन्ति । तेषां सर्वेषां जात्यन्तरजातानां जातीनां कर्माणि च प्रतिपादितानि सन्ति । द्विजातयश्चोपनयनादिक्रियालोपेन यजनाध्ययनप्रायाश्चित्तादीनाञ्चाभावेन शनैः शूद्रतां गच्छन्ति । तेषु च पौण्ड्रक–चौड्र–द्रविड–काम्बोज–यवन–शक–पारद–पल्हव–चीन–किरात–दरद–खसाः क्रियालोपादिना शूद्रत्वमापन्ना मन्यन्ते । तेषां सर्वेषां संक्षिप्तविवरणमध्ययनेऽस्मिन् समुपस्थापितमस्ति । तत्र च गृहस्थानां वर्णानां प्राणयात्रार्थं दायाद्याः सप्त धनागमा धम्र्या मन्यन्ते । तेषां जीवनार्थं विद्याशिल्पादयो दश जीवनहेतवश्च निर्देशिताः सन्ति ।
american_english: There are four varnas, beginning with the Brahmin. The description of the varna system is found prescribed everywhere in texts such as the Vedas, Smritis and Puranas. Among the varnas following the householder stage of life, six acts are prescribed in the shastras for Brahmins: the teaching and studying of the Veda together with its auxiliary sciences, performing yajnas and officiating at them, and giving and receiving gifts. Of those acts, three — officiating at yajnas, teaching and receiving — are considered the means of livelihood for Brahmins. Likewise, three acts — the study of the Veda, performing yajna and giving — are prescribed as duties for Kshatriyas too, just as for Brahmins. The three acts known as teaching, officiating at yajna and receiving are considered forbidden for Kshatriyas. For Kshatriyas, the chief act, both for livelihood and for dharma, is prescribed to be only the protection of the people. Similarly, for the Vaishya, yajna, study and giving, and kusida, agriculture, trade and the rearing of cattle are considered livelihoods. For the Shudra, however, the chief act for the sake of dharma and livelihood is considered by the authors of the dharma-shastras to be only the service of the twice-born. In this way, when one cannot live by the acts prescribed in the shastras, provision is made in the dharma-shastras for apad-dharma, the law of emergency. In that emergency, a Brahmin may act by the acts of a Kshatriya, a Kshatriya by the acts of a Vaishya, and the Vaishya also may act by the acts of a Shudra. Likewise, provision is made that even a Shudra, unable to live by the service of the twice-born, may live by various crafts. Within the varnas, the jati system is also shown. There, among the twelve types of sons born within the varnas, only the son born — in accordance with the marriage procedure prescribed in the shastra — of a wedded wife of the same varna, the aurasa son, is considered same-varna and of the same jati. In the anuloma marriages of the varnas, six anuloma-born sons are produced in sequence: Murdhavasikta, Ambastha, Nishada, Mahishya, Ugra and Karana. There is no rule for pratiloma marriage in the dharma-shastra. Nevertheless, six pratiloma-born sons also exist there: Suta, Vaidehaka, Chandala, Magadha, Kshatta and Ayogava. From daughters of mixed castes married among themselves are born the various sons such as Pukkasa, Kukkutaka, Kshetta, Shvapaka, Vena, Sairindhra, Maitreya, Margava, Charmakar, Andhra, Meda, Sopaka, Antyavasayin, Pandusopaka and Ahindaka. The prescribed acts of all these castes born of inter-varna unions are also expounded. And the dvijas, by neglect of rites such as upanayana and by absence of yajna, study and prayashchitta, gradually pass into Shudrahood. Among them, the Paundr(aka), Chaudra, Dravida, Kamboja, Yavana, Shaka, Parada, Pallava, China, Kirata, Darada and Khasa are considered to have attained Shudrahood through neglect of rites and the like. A brief account of all of them is presented in this study. There, for varnas living in the householder stage, seven ways of acquiring wealth, beginning with inheritance, are considered dharmya, i.e. lawful, for the sake of sustaining life. Ten means of livelihood, beginning with vidya and shilpa, are also prescribed as means of living for them.

translator_notes: Source text is Sanskrit printed in Devanagari in the 'nepali' field; the damaged glyphs 'वृ¤यर्थं' are read as वृत्त्यर्थ ('for livelihood'), with the same corruption repeated elsewhere. 'कुसीद' (listed among Vaishya livelihoods) is unidentified and transliterated as 'kusida' rather than guessed. 'क्षेत्ता' is transliterated as printed (likely क्षत्ता). Source spells शुद्र without long ū and uses 'पौण्ड्रक' etc.; name lists are kept as printed/transliterated, not normalised. Sentence order preserved as in the source. Informal variant rendered in NZ casual flavour.
